title: Mar Zutra of Drishba

paragraphs: [Bava Batra 126b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.126b.3) relates that he was a firstborn who divided a basket of pepper equally with his brothers. He came before Rav Ashi, who told him, “Since you have waived your right in part, you have waived it with respect to all the property.” The commentator Hyman cites as [R. G.](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Gershom_on_Bava_Batra.126b.3) explains the name as a place-name. Hyman reports that [Dikdukei Soferim](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/ASiAqDXazUEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=RA1-PA350) reads Mar Zutra Rushba.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s printed page has ר״ג. The supplied Hebrew transcription has ר״נ. The linked gloss transmitted under Rabbeinu Gershom explains Drishba as a place-name.
The linked Dikdukei Soferim, p. 350, note 9, has Mar bar Rushba in the manuscript column. Hyman reports the name more briefly as Mar Zutra Rushba.
The case concerns the firstborn’s waiver of his additional share. The brothers divided the basket of pepper equally.
